mstts:express-as.prosody: Imagine walking through the vast corridors of Western history, where every painting, every idea, and every belief has been shaped by the questions people have asked for centuries. Have you ever wondered how societies decide what truly matters—or how those decisions ripple through generations? Together, we’re about to embark on a journey that explores how philosophy, art, science, and religion have danced together—sometimes in harmony, sometimes in conflict—to create the world we know today. In Francis A. Schaeffer’s How Should We Then Live? The Rise and Decline of Western Thought and Culture, we’ll uncover those critical turning points—moments when a shift in worldview didn’t just change ideas, but actually steered the course of entire nations and touched the lives of ordinary people like you and me. Picture the splendor of ancient Rome, the bold strokes of Renaissance artists, and the stormy debates that echoed through the twentieth century. Each era built on the hopes and questions of the one before it—sometimes embracing new answers, sometimes pushing back with all its might. What’s fascinating is how these waves of change didn’t just stay in the realm of the abstract, but shaped laws, politics, and even the way people lived out their everyday lives. As we dig deeper, we’ll see why understanding these patterns isn’t just interesting—it’s urgent, especially as we navigate our own fast-changing world. So, welcome to this journey. Let’s explore together what it means to live wisely and with purpose, guided by the lessons woven through the story of Western thought and culture.
